Collaborate

The next question.
Let’s ask it together.

We welcome researchers, clinicians, engineers and industry partners. Bring a new method or perspective to a question that starts with the skin.

These discussion topics grow from our published research. A specific study can take shape around our shared questions and complementary expertise.

Academic collaboration ↗Industry collaboration ↗
01 / Epigenetic Skin Aging

From aging regulators to tissue responses

Can epigenetic regulation explain variation in skin-aging responses across donors and environments?

Experience we bring
Published work in human skin, fibroblast models, senescence mechanisms and transcriptome integration
Complementary expertise
Epigenomics, quantitative biology and tissue-level validation
Discuss this question ↗Related research story →
02 / Inflammatory Skin Disease

Cell states and treatment response in AD

Can joint analysis of immune-cell states in blood and skin help explain disease heterogeneity and treatment response?

Experience we bring
Collaborative work connecting clinical questions, single-cell analysis, high-dimensional immune profiling and functional assays
Complementary expertise
Clinical researchers, single-cell and bioinformatics expertise, longitudinal study design
Discuss this question ↗Related research story →
03 / Skin–Brain Interaction

Routes from skin signals to systemic effects

Can local skin responses be separated from systemic mediators to test skin–brain communication?

Experience we bring
Collaborative experience connecting skin UV-exposure models with pharmacological and functional analyses
Complementary expertise
Neurophysiology, metabolite analysis and signaling mechanisms
Discuss this question ↗Related research story →
04 / Medical Devices & EBD

Measuring responses to devices and EBD

Can energy-delivery conditions and biological skin responses be connected through objective imaging and evaluation?

Experience we bring
Experience in clinical assessment of energy-based treatments, quantitative skin imaging and collaborations connecting clinical questions with engineering approaches
Complementary expertise
Device and optical engineering, quantitative imaging, data analysis and industry R&D
Discuss this question ↗Related research area →
